gist: A couple who used to clean each other's homes before marriage concludes they were destined for each other, punning on maid and made.

characters.looks: middle-aged man, casual shirt, smug grin
woman with rubber gloves and a mop

wordplay.explanation: 'maid for each other' sounds like 'made for each other'; maid = cleaning servant.

de.note: maid/made homophone has no German equivalent

gist: A man claims a diagnosed phobia of giants whose name is built from the giant's fairy-tale chant.

wordplay.explanation: 'FeeFiphobia' blends the giant's chant 'Fee-fi-fo-fum' with 'phobia'.

cultureRefs: Jack and the Beanstalk giant's chant 'Fee-fi-fo-fum'

de.note: chant unknown in German, pun lost

gist: Asks whether photographic memory is innate or takes time to develop, punning on developing photographs.

wordplay.explanation: 'develop' = grow over time and develop photographic film.

gist: Counting sex partners as twosome and threesome leads to an insult that 'handsome' means having sex alone with your hand.

characters.looks: cocky young guy, smirk, casual hoodie

wordplay.explanation: 'handsome' split as 'hand-some', a sex act with one's own hand, following twosome/threesome.

gist: Dads tell dad jokes to watch their kids grow up, punning on the groans the jokes provoke.

wordplay.explanation: 'groan up' sounds like 'grown up'; groaning at bad jokes.

gist: Asked which doctor he will call, dad hears 'witch doctor' and answers that he means the regular kind.

characters.looks: middle-aged woman, puzzled look, coffee mug

wordplay.explanation: 'Which doctor?' heard as 'witch doctor', a tribal healer.

gist: A house wears 'a dress', punning on its address.

wordplay.explanation: 'Address' sounds like 'a dress'.

characters.looks: lonely nerdy guy in sci-fi t-shirt

wordplay.explanation: 'Alderaan places' sounds like 'all the wrong places'; Alderaan is a Star Wars planet.

cultureRefs: song 'Lookin' for Love (in All the Wrong Places)'

gist: Claims French fries were first cooked in Greece, punning on grease.

wordplay.explanation: 'Greece' sounds like 'grease' used for frying.

gist: An injured cat speaking as 'Me' says 'Ow', spelling out a meow.

wordplay.explanation: 'Me: Ow' reads as 'Meow' while also meaning the speaker says 'Ow'.

de.note: spelling trick works only in English

gist: Compares women to grenades: take off the ring and you lose the house, the ring being both pin and wedding ring.

wordplay.explanation: 'ring' = grenade pull ring and wedding ring; removing it ends in divorce losing the house.

gist: A song costing 45 cents is one by a 50-cent artist featuring a band whose name suggests a nickel back as change.

wordplay.explanation: '50 Cent' (rapper) and 'Nickelback' (band) read as 50 cents minus a nickel back = 45 cents.

ru.note: depends on English artist names and US coins

de.note: depends on English artist names and US coins

gist: Someone addicted to films with strong female leads is called a heroine addict, punning on heroin.

wordplay.explanation: 'heroine' (female lead) sounds like 'heroin' (drug).

gist: A man says a sign made him wet himself, as if from laughter, but the sign said the toilets were closed.

wordplay.explanation: 'made me piss myself' = laughed hard and literally wet himself because the toilet was closed.

de.note: 'mir in die Hose gemacht' works both ways

gist: A statistics lesson that larger samples give reliable averages ends with the idiom about ends justifying means, with N for sample size.

characters.looks: nerdy student with glasses and notebook

wordplay.explanation: 'The N's justify the means': N = sample size, means = averages, echoing 'the ends justify the means'.

ru.note: idiom and N/ends sound pun lost

de.note: idiom and N/ends sound pun lost

gist: Warns against a pillow fight with Death because of the consequences, punning repercussions as reaper cushions.

characters.looks: hooded skeleton with scythe, holding pillow

wordplay.explanation: 'reaper cushions' sounds like 'repercussions'.

gist: Says communism's failure was foreseeable from all its red flags, literal and figurative.

wordplay.explanation: 'red flags' = warning signs and literal communist red flags.

ru.note: 'red flag' as warning sign is a recent loan; may need framing

de.note: 'Red Flags' as warning sign is a loan; may need framing

gist: Asked if their kids are spoiled, a husband answers that they just smell that way, taking spoiled as rotten.

wordplay.explanation: 'spoiled' = pampered and rotten (smelling bad).

gist: Asks whether buttcheeks is written as one word or should be spread apart, mixing spelling with anatomy.

wordplay.explanation: 'spread them apart' = write as separate words and physically spread the buttocks.

gist: A would-be teacher will only teach subtraction because he wants to make a difference, the mathematical result of subtraction.

characters.looks: earnest young teacher, sweater vest, chalk

wordplay.explanation: 'make a difference' = have impact and compute a difference by subtracting.

gist: Two laughing helium atoms sound like 'HeHe', the element symbol repeated.

wordplay.explanation: He is helium's chemical symbol; 'HeHe' reads as laughter.

gist: A customer tells a hovering tuxedo-store clerk to leave him alone, and the clerk replies with a suit pun.

characters.nameInText: The guy at the tuxedo store
characters.looks: slick clerk, tape measure around neck

wordplay.explanation: 'Suit yourself' = do as you like, and suit = formal outfit.

gist: Believing in one eighth of the Bible makes him an 'eighth theist', a sound pun on atheist.

characters.looks: casual guy holding a Bible, shrugging

wordplay.explanation: 'eighth theist' sounds like 'atheist'; 12.5% = one eighth.

gist: Comparing apple pie prices across islands yields 'pie rates of the Caribbean', a pun on pirates.

wordplay.explanation: 'pie rates' sounds like 'pirates', echoing the film title Pirates of the Caribbean.

gist: A man threatens the thief who stole his glasses that he will find him because he has contacts, meaning lenses.

characters.looks: squinting man, menacing pose, no glasses

characters.nameInText: the person who stole my glasses
characters.looks: sneaky thief in mask holding glasses

wordplay.explanation: 'contacts' = useful connections and contact lenses.

gist: Grandpa wants his ashes turned into a diamond, and the family calls it a lot of pressure, both emotional and diamond-forming.

characters.looks: cheerful old man pointing at a diamond ring

wordplay.explanation: 'pressure' = emotional burden and the physical pressure that makes diamonds.

de.note: 'ganz schön viel Druck' works both ways

gist: Told his wife and daughter look like sisters, a man says they were separated at birth, literally true of mother and child.

characters.looks: youthful woman, same hair as daughter

wordplay.explanation: 'separated at birth' = lookalike siblings idiom and literal separation of mother and newborn.

gist: Claims Canada is fake because it was all 'mapleleaf', a pun on make-believe.

wordplay.explanation: 'mapleleaf' sounds like 'make-believe'.

gist: A man wants to sue the airline over damaged luggage, and the lawyer says he does not have much of a case, meaning suitcase.

characters.looks: angry traveler holding a crushed suitcase
lawyer in suit behind desk, smirking

wordplay.explanation: 'case' = legal case and suitcase.

gist: Karate for amputees is called partial arts, a pun on martial arts.

wordplay.explanation: 'partial arts' sounds like 'martial arts'; partial refers to missing limbs.

gist: A passenger in the last row hopes for chicken breast but expects only sausage left, punning best/worst.

characters.looks: cramped passenger in last row, anxious

wordplay.explanation: 'hoping for the breast, preparing for the wurst' echoes 'hope for the best, prepare for the worst'.

gist: A father puts his daughter's photo in a locket for her 18th birthday and says she is 'independent', i.e. in the pendant.

characters.looks: emotional dad, teary eyes, holding locket

wordplay.explanation: 'independent' heard as 'in the pendant', where her picture sits.

gist: An epitaph for evaporated boiling water says it will be mist, a pun on missed.

wordplay.explanation: 'mist' sounds like 'missed'.

gist: The letter C fears the other letters because they are 'Not-Cs', sounding like Nazis.

wordplay.explanation: 'Not-Cs' sounds like 'Nazis'.

gist: The longest word is 'smiles' because there is a mile between its first and last letters.

wordplay.explanation: 'smiles' spelled S-mile-S, a mile between the two S's.

gist: A man suspects his wife is gluing his gun collection and, despite her denial, sticks to his guns.

characters.looks: suspicious man, hands stuck to a rifle

wordplay.explanation: 'sticking to my guns' = holding his position and literally stuck by glue.

gist: The difference between a formally dressed cyclist and a casual unicyclist is attire, i.e. a tire.

wordplay.explanation: 'Attire' sounds like 'a tire'.

gist: More bullies at a school means the mean increases, mean being both average and nasty.

wordplay.explanation: 'mean' = statistical average and cruel.

gist: A man says his drone stuck in a tree is not the worst thing today but it is definitely up there, literally.

characters.looks: frustrated man holding a remote, looking up

wordplay.explanation: 'up there' = high on the list and physically up in the tree.

gist: A man compulsively telling airport jokes is told by his doctor that his condition is terminal.

wordplay.explanation: 'terminal' = fatal illness and airport terminal.

gist: A friend asks 'what's upstairs' and the host takes it as a greeting to the stairs, replying that stairs don't talk.

wordplay.explanation: 'what's upstairs' heard as 'what's up, stairs' greeting.

gist: Arrested for stealing electrons, a man is heavily charged though victims call it positive, all electricity puns.

characters.looks: man in handcuffs, hair standing up from static

wordplay.explanation: 'charged' = accused and electrically charged; 'positive' = good and positive charge.

gist: Asked to stop singing a famous song to his wife, a husband answers with the song's well-known lyric word.

characters.looks: angry teen girl with school backpack
calm dad in armchair lowering newspaper

gist: Nurses carry red crayons in case they need to draw blood, as in drawing a picture.

characters.looks: nurse in scrubs holding a red crayon

wordplay.explanation: 'draw blood' = take a blood sample and draw a picture of blood.

gist: Dad lies on the floor claiming a mysterious force pulls him down and asks his wife if she grasps the gravity of the situation.

characters.looks: dad sprawled on floor, dramatic face
exasperated woman with hands on hips

wordplay.explanation: 'gravity' = seriousness and gravitational force.

wordplay.explanation: 'Well prayed' = 'well played' with a stereotyped Chinese l/r accent.

gist: Someone asks if anyone wants to be his companion, 'asking for a friend', literally wanting a friend.

characters.looks: lonely guy with hopeful puppy eyes

wordplay.explanation: 'asking for a friend' = covering for oneself and literally requesting a friend.

gist: A driver admits it is unsafe to drive but says bad brakes have never stopped him.

wordplay.explanation: 'never stopped me' = never deterred me and brakes failed to stop the car.

gist: A man avoids greeting his ex across a museum hall because there is too much history between them, both personal and exhibits.

characters.looks: awkward man hiding behind a statue
woman viewing exhibits across the hall

wordplay.explanation: 'history between us' = shared past and literal historical exhibits between them.
